AcmeCorp-NOC: Hey team — since ~09:10 UTC our app calls to https://api.redwood.ai are failing only when traffic goes through our corporate proxy. Direct egress works fine. We see 502 / connection reset from app. Repro steps below, any quick checks?

AcmeCorp-NOC: repro (from app host):
```
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\"
*   Trying 10.0.0.1...
* Connected to corp-proxy (10.0.0.1) port 8080 (#0)
> CONNECT api.redwood.ai:443 HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai:443
> Proxy-Connection: Keep-Alive
>
< HTTP/1.1 200 Connection established
< Proxy-agent: corpfw/5.2

* SSL connection using TLSv1.3 / TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384
* TLS handshake has read 0 bytes and written 2048 bytes
* SSL: connection reset by peer
* Closing connection 0
curl: (56) OpenSSL SSL_read: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL, errno 104
```

Ana (Support): Thanks — can you confirm the proxy vendor/version and whether it does TLS inspection (MITM)? Also can you try openssl s_client to see the ClientHello/ServerHello behavior? Any gateway logs?

AcmeCorp-NOC: Proxy is \"CorpFW v5.2\" (security team manages it). They say it does TLS bumping for inspected hosts and will replace certs. Here's a quick openssl run we tried:
```
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -alpn h2 -tlsextdebug
CONNECTED(00000003)
140123456789120:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s23_clnt.c:770:
---
No peer certificate available
---
```

Maria (NetOps): That handshake failure + reset after CONNECT + proxy-agent header looks like the proxy terminates TLS and then something rewrites the SNI/host. If the proxy replaces the SNI with an internal DNS name it can route to an internal pool that doesn't respond properly, causing the reset. Can you capture the TLS ClientHello from the proxy side? If not, run this from a laptop outside the proxy to compare.

Ryan (Eng Oncall): From Redwood's side we require SNI and ALPN to select the right cert and route to the inference fleet. If the proxy is removing SNI or rewriting it to an internal hostname our frontends won't match and the connection can be dropped or routed to a generic endpoint that rejects multiplexed HTTP/2. Two quick checks: 1) does the proxy preserve the original SNI in the ClientHello when forwarding, and 2) does it preserve ALPN h2 or http/1.1?

Ryan (Eng Oncall): If you can run a pcap, look for the TLS ClientHello's server_name extension. Example tcpdump filter to capture handshake bytes:
```
sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -s 0 -w /tmp/redwood-hello.pcap host api.redwood.ai and port 443
```
Open the pcap in Wireshark and inspect ClientHello -> Extensions -> server_name.

AcmeCorp-NOC: We pulled a small pcap and verified — the ClientHello leaving the proxy has SNI = "internal-inspect.corp.local" (proxy replaced host), not api.redwood.ai. Also ALPN shows no h2, only http/1.1. Security team is doing aggressive MITM and also forcing ALPN downgrade.

Ana (Support): That explains it. Our frontends rely on SNI to select the cert and ALPN to enable h2+multiplexing. When SNI is rewritten we sometimes end up in a catch-all route that doesn't accept the proxied connections, or the altered cert chain fails verification and the proxy tears down the socket. Two remediation options:
- Short term: have security add api.redwood.ai to the proxy's TLS passthrough/allowlist so CONNECT is forwarded without MITM. This preserves SNI and ALPN.
- Mid term: configure the proxy to preserve original SNI and ALPN when inspection is required (some vendors support preserving the ClientHello and performing inspection on a copy).
- Alternative workaround: route Redwood API traffic via a dedicated egress IP that the proxy can allowlist by IP rather than hostname.

Maria (NetOps): Security is hesitant but will propose a scoped exception for api.redwood.ai only for service account IP ranges. Also looking into proxy config option \"bump-exempt list\". Any specific header/host checks we should avoid so proxy doesn't rewrite?

Ryan (Eng Oncall): Important: do NOT convert the CONNECT into an HTTP request or inject HTML/headers after CONNECT 200. CONNECT must remain a raw TCP tunnel for TLS. If the proxy injects headers or terminates then re-issues a new request, that breaks TLS. Also ensure they don't rewrite SNI to an internal name. If you need to inspect, use a mirrored-decrypt approach or preserve the SNI.

AcmeCorp-NOC: Understood. Security will try the passthrough for our service account IPs and test. Any testing tips?

Ana (Support): After the allowlist is in place: from an affected host run the same curl command and confirm you now see a normal TLS handshake and a 200/stream from /v1/generate. Example quick test:
```
curl -v -x http://corp-proxy:8080 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/healthz
# should return HTTP/1.1 200 OK and not SSL reset
```
If you still see issues, grab a tcpdump and send the pcap to support (redact sensitive data).

AcmeCorp-NOC: Security made the scoped exception and verified passthrough for our IPs. Confirmed a successful curl health check, and our app traffic is green again. Thanks everyone! :tada:

Ryan (Eng Oncall): Glad it's resolved. If you want we can add a note to our private deployment docs about proxy interception gotchas (SNI/ALPN/preserve CONNECT).

Ana (Support): Marking this thread resolved. If the customer wants a short KB we can draft one with commands and exact proxy config hints. :thumbsup:
